subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE PROLOGUE-SHADOW AXIS OF THE ADDR16_LO HOME-COPY CLASS IS CLOSED BY DIRECT EXPERIMENT, NOT BY INFERENCE. claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v1 FINDING 3 calls over-hoisting and the home copy 'ONE event, observationally inseparable', and claim.law.addr16-lo-home-copy-census-no-source-discriminant.20260831.v1 FINDING 3 argues the shadow is downstream from the statistic 'the target places a callee-saved-homed ADDR16_LO addi in the prologue shadow 0 times in 683 (it structurally cannot)'. THAT STATISTIC IS A TAUTOLOGY: a callee-saved-homed addi in the shadow is shape A by definition and impossible by construction, so 0/683 carries no information about causal direction, and this run reproduced the same vacuous cell on OUR side (OURS shape-A addi-in-shadow 0 of 888). The two halves ARE separable, and one build separates them.

THE EXPERIMENT. `#pragma scheduling off` / `#pragma scheduling reset` around a single function is RECOGNISED by this toolchain's MWCC 1.2.5 (it is not silently ignored: the object bytes move, and the prologue shadow empties completely). Run on two P-roster functions in two TUs:

  game/world/world::StartWorldLoad -- baseline real 63, insns T122/O123, multiset 1t `ours-only: -1 mr`, fuzzy 97.3361%. With scheduling off: real 99, insns T122/O123, multiset 1t, STILL `ours-only: -1 mr`. `fndiff --ops` shows `delete T[1:2]@4-8=['lis'] O[1:1]@4-4=[]` -- our `lis` has left the shadow entirely -- and the copy is still there at O[7:9]=['mr','lis'].

  game/mb/mb_model::MBOX_BGLoadModelStart -- baseline real 46, insns T71/O71, multiset 2t (`target-only: +1 add  ours-only: -1 mr`), fuzzy 87.8873%. With scheduling off: real 64, fuzzy 54.0704%, insns T71/O71, multiset 2t, STILL `ours-only: -1 mr`. The aligned prologue (`fnasm game/mb/mb_model MBOX_BGLoadModelStart 0x0:0x2c --ours`) reads `@0x0 mflr r0` / `@0x4 stw r0,4(r1)` / `@0x8 stwu r1,-48(r1)` / `@0xc stmw r26,24(r1)` / `@0x10 addi r31,r3,0` / `@0x14 addi r26,r4,0` / `@0x18 lis r3,lbl_80115DA8@ha` / `@0x1c addi r0,r3,lbl_80115DA8@lo` / `@0x20 mr r28,r0` / `@0x24 lis r3,lbl_802A5CF0@ha` / `@0x28 addi r29,r3,lbl_802A5CF0@lo`. NOTHING is hoisted -- the frame is set up at `@0x8` and r28 is saved at `@0xc` -- and MWCC STILL routes the low half through r0 at `@0x1c` and pays `mr r28,r0` at `@0x20`.

THE LAW. The ADDR16_LO home copy is emitted even when the @lo addi sits AFTER the frame save with the callee-saved home provably writable. Therefore prologue-shadow placement CANNOT be the cause of the copy; it is a downstream consequence of the destination already being volatile, and the entire over-hoisting axis is unavailable as a cure for the 21-function shadow subclass. This is the same conclusion AD reached, reached soundly.

THE WITHIN-FUNCTION CONTROL, which is the strongest single observation of the run. In that scheduling-off MBOX_BGLoadModelStart prologue, TWO file-scope addresses are materialised back to back under one identical schedule, one frame and one register pressure: lbl_80115DA8 pays the copy (shape B, `@0x1c addi r0,r3,lbl_80115DA8@lo` + `@0x20 mr r28,r0`) and lbl_802A5CF0 does not (shape A, `@0x28 addi r29,r3,lbl_802A5CF0@lo`). Same function, same prologue, same instant, opposite outcomes. No property of the function -- schedule, frame, shadow, save style, leaf-ness, pressure, flags or compiler build, i.e. every one of AD's twelve axes -- can discriminate two sites that share all of them. The discriminating variable is per-VALUE, and in this instance the loser is the address bound FIRST in source order (`char* strs = (char*)lbl_80115DA8;` at the top of the declaration block) while the winner is bound later (`tbl = lbl_802A5CF0;` as the first statement).

TOOL FACT, recorded because it is a general instrument and the corpus did not have it: `#pragma scheduling off` is live in this MWCC and isolates scheduler effects from allocator effects at the cost of one build. Any residual whose diagnosis names the scheduler can now be tested directly instead of argued about -- if the residual survives the pragma, the scheduler is not its cause.
